questions.q: What kind of animals were Ginger and Pickles?
choices: A yellow tom-cat and a terrier
A brown rabbit and a mouse
A tabby cat and a collie dog
A gray rat and a dormouse
questions.evidence: Ginger was a yellow tom-cat, and Pickles was a terrier.

questions.q: Why did Ginger ask Pickles to serve the mice?
choices: The mice made his mouth water
Pickles was much better at sums
The mice only liked to talk to dogs
Ginger was always too busy eating
questions.evidence: because he said it made his mouth water

questions.q: In the story, what does buying on "credit" mean?
choices: Paying twice as much money
Saying you will pay another time
Getting something for half price
Trading one thing for another
questions.evidence: she says she will pay another time

questions.q: Why was there never any money in the till?
choices: Robbers came and stole it
The customers never paid
Ginger spent it all on fish
Nobody came to the shop
questions.evidence: they never paid for as much as a pennyworth of peppermints

questions.q: What could Pickles not buy because there was no money?
choices: A new collar
A dog licence
A bag of biscuits
A warm coat
questions.evidence: Pickles was unable to buy a dog licence

questions.q: Who was the policeman who came into the shop?
choices: A real live policeman
A German doll
Samuel Whiskers in a helmet
Kep the Collie dog

questions.q: What did Ginger and Pickles do after they opened the envelope?
choices: Closed up the shop and left
Paid all the bills at once
Sent the bills to everybody again
Gave the shop to Tabitha Twitchit

questions.q: Who opened the shop again at the end of the story?
choices: Tabitha Twitchit
Mr. John Dormouse
Sally Henny Penny
Timothy Baker
questions.evidence: Sally Henny Penny sent out a printed poster to say that she was going to re-open the shop

questions.q: What is this story mostly about?
choices: A shop that closes because nobody pays for anything
A cat and a dog who fight over a bar of soap
A policeman who catches robbers in the village
A hen who sells candles and peppermints to mice
questions.evidence: As there was always no money, Ginger and Pickles were obliged to eat their own goods.
